headline: GENUS POWER: Ganesh Kashyap, ex-CEO of Landis+Gyr India, appointed President-Software Business (senior management), effective 17 Nov 2026
facts: Appointment of Mr. Ganesh Kashyap as President-Software Business, category Senior Management Personnel
Effective date 17 November 2026; one person reported
Most recent role: CEO & Whole Time Director at Landis+Gyr India
Profile cites over 35 years of experience across the US and India, with earlier stints at HCL Technologies and DRDO India
Stated expertise: AI, IoT, Smart Grid, Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI), telecom
Not an outcome of a board meeting; no remuneration, notice period or reason for the vacancy is given
read: This is a senior hire into a software role at a smart-metering company. He comes from Landis+Gyr, which makes smart meters and so competes in the same field. It suggests Genus wants to build its software and AMI layer. It is a single senior appointment, not a change in revenue, orders or capital, so it is small against the company. The filing gives no figures, so any effect on earnings is unknown.
positives: Relevant AMI and smart-grid experience from a direct industry peer
Points to investment in software and the recurring-revenue side of metering
Senior outside hire adds depth below the promoter team
risks: The filing has no numbers, and the benefit depends on how well he executes
A software president is a new or newly filled role, and the filing does not say whether it replaces someone
Possible non-compete or conflict issues from moving from a competitor, which the filing does not mention
check_next: Whether the post is new or replaces someone, and what the software business earns in revenue and margin
His remuneration, ESOPs and notice terms, and any non-compete with Landis+Gyr
What management says about software and AMI on the next earnings call, and any other senior exits
price_context: The stock closed at 276.85, 30.3% below its high and down 21.7% in 3 months, with RSI 41.9 and volume at 0.8 times normal. It is in a weak trend and the filing, which came after market hours, had not been priced in.

headline: REFEX: bags NTPC Tamil Nadu Energy Co. pond ash utilisation contract, max award value Rs. 28,00,00,000 over 2 years
facts: Awarded by NTPC Tamil Nadu Energy Company Limited, a domestic, unlisted counterparty. It is a Joint Venture of NTPC Limited (NSE: NTPC).
Nature of contract: Contract for Pond Ash Utilization. Scope of supply and services: Utilization of Pond Ash.
Amount of the order is 280000000 INR. The consideration reads 'Cumulative Maximum Award Value of Rs. 28,00,00,000 (excl. all taxes and duties)'.
The contract is valid for a period of two (2) years.
Dated 2026-11-16, event time 17:55:00. The company says it is ordinary course of business, not a related-party transaction, and that promoters have no interest in the awarding entity.
read: Read: this is a small, ordinary-course order from a creditworthy PSU joint venture, spread over two years. The filing gives no company revenue, so I cannot size it against sales. The wording 'Cumulative Maximum Award Value' means the Rs. 28,00,00,000 is a ceiling, not a committed order. It adds to the ash-handling business line but does not change the investment case on its own.
positives: Counterparty is an NTPC joint venture, so payment risk looks low (read, not stated in the filing)
Not a related-party deal, with no promoter interest declared
Adds repeat-type ash utilisation work with a defined two-year term
risks: The value is a maximum, so actual billing could be lower
No margin, volume or rate disclosed, so profit impact is unknown
Over two years the annual run-rate is small, and the filing does not say how much of this the company already does for NTPC
check_next: Compare the Rs. 28,00,00,000 ceiling with Refex's latest annual and quarterly revenue and its existing order book
Check the contract terms: minimum quantity, pricing mechanism, payment cycle and penalties
Check the margin on ash and coal-handling work against the company's reported EBITDA margin, and whether the company tends to report orders at their ceiling value
price_context: The stock is weak: close 224.26, 39.9% below its high, down 24.0% over 3 months, RSI 38.7, volume 1.1 times normal and delivery 35.0%, so the order is not yet moving the price and the trend is still down.

headline: NEWGEN: Wins Ghana credit management software order worth USD 2,345,208 (INR 21.94 Crore), 3-year execution
facts: Customer is an overseas entity in Ghana, West Africa. The name is withheld for confidentiality.
Order value is USD 2,345,208, shown as INR 21.94 Crore at 1 USD = INR 93.57.

Scope: Automated Credit Management Solution on the Newgen Platform. It covers software licensing, design, development and implementation, a Gen AI & Data Science subscription, and AMC and support in Years 2 and 3.
To be executed over 3 years.
The filing says the order is in the ordinary course of business. It says the customer is not a related party and that promoters have no interest in the customer.
Order date is 2026-11-17.
read: This is a routine-sized international win for the core platform. The filing does not give Newgen's revenue, so the order cannot be measured against the company's size here. At INR 21.94 Crore spread over 3 years, the yearly revenue is probably small for a listed software company, but that is an inference and not from the filing. It adds to evidence that the Gen AI and data science offering is being sold, but it does not change the investment case.
positives: Clean order: not a related party, and the promoters have no interest in the customer
Multi-year deal that includes recurring subscription and AMC and support
Shows continued international demand, here in Africa
risks: Customer is unnamed, so its credit quality and payment risk are unknown
Value is spread over 3 years, with licence revenue likely front-loaded and AMC only in Years 2 and 3
The filing gives no split between licence, subscription and services, so margin and timing are unclear
check_next: Compare INR 21.94 Crore with Newgen's trailing revenue and its recent order-win and deal-size history
Check how much of the order is licence revenue recognised upfront versus subscription and AMC
Check the Ghana receivable and payment terms, and the USD/INR exposure, in the next results and annual report
price_context: The stock closed at 427.55, which is 60.1% below its high, down 25.0% over 3 months, with RSI 30.2 and volume at 0.6 times normal, so it is in a downtrend (a stage 4 chart) and this small order has not changed that.

headline: HCC: CHRO Jyotirmoy Banerjee resigns effective 2026-11-17; Vivek Kumar Dubey appointed CHRO from 2026-12-08
facts: Jyotirmoy Banerjee, Chief Human Resources Officer (Senior Management Personnel), resigned; resignation letter received and effective 2026-11-17
Reason given: to pursue new challenges and opportunities that align more closely with his long-term career goals
Mr. Vivek Kumar Dubey appointed Chief Human Resources Officer (Senior Management Personnel), effective 2026-12-08
Dubey has over 26 years in HR; was Group CHRO at Vishvaraj Group; earlier roles at Jindal Water Infrastructure, Larsen & Toubro, Shristi Group, Synefra Engineering & Construction and Abhijeet Group
Not an outcome of a board meeting; the filing shows the term of appointment as 0 months, with no term stated
read: This is a routine swap of one senior HR officer for another. The CHRO is senior management, not a KMP like the CEO or CFO. It does not change orders, balance sheet or earnings. The gap between 2026-11-17 and 2026-12-08 leaves the post without a named holder for about three weeks, which is minor.
positives: Replacement already named, with 26 years of HR experience in infrastructure and engineering
Resignation reason is stated as career-related, with no dispute cited
risks: Departure is effective immediately, with the successor starting 2026-12-08
One more senior exit; the filing alone cannot show whether it is part of a pattern
Stock is weak, so any further senior exits would draw more attention
check_next: Check how many KMP and SMP exits HCC has filed in the last 12 months
Read the resignation letter and any further disclosure the filing says will follow
Confirm who covers HR duties until 2026-12-08

headline: REFEX: bags pond ash utilisation contract from an unnamed 'Major Power Producer Company', max award value Rs. 28,00,00,000, valid 2 years

The filing doesn't name the client. The NTPC Tamil Nadu Energy Co. label in my earlier note comes from the file name and the earlier read, not from the filing text. This repeats my earlier read of the same filing and adds nothing new. It is a modest, clean, non-related-party order, and the filing gives no margin or volume to judge its profit.
positives: Domestic order from a large power producer, with a stated 2-year term
Not a related party deal, and no promoter interest in the client
Adds to Refex's ash-handling work, though the filing doesn't say how large that business is
risks: 'Maximum' award value is not a committed order, so actual billing could be lower
Client is unnamed and no margin, tonnage or payment terms are given
No revenue figure was provided, so materiality can't be measured; the filing gives no profit contribution

headline: INDIA GLYCOLS: First post-demerger Q2 FY27 results: revenue Rs. 358.18 Cr, EBITDA Rs. 39.34 Cr, PAT Rs. 11.24 Cr; prior year not comparable
facts: Q2 FY27 unaudited standalone: revenue from operations Rs. 358.18 crore, EBITDA Rs. 39.34 crore, PAT Rs. 11.24 crore, quarterly EPS Rs. 1.68.
Q1 FY27 (restated for the demerger): revenue Rs. 354.64 crore, EBITDA Rs. 40.21 crore, PAT Rs. 12.35 crore, EPS Rs. 1.84.
H1 FY27: revenue Rs. 712.82 crore, EBITDA Rs. 79.55 crore, PAT Rs. 23.59 crore, EPS Rs. 3.52.

Q2 FY26 comparatives (Rs. 2,410.71 crore revenue, Rs. 160.25 crore EBITDA, Rs. 53.94 crore PAT) include the demerged Spirits & Biofuel and Biopharma undertakings. The company says they are not comparable.

The NCLT Allahabad Bench approved the Scheme on July 17, 2026. It became effective on September 1, 2026, with an appointed date of April 1, 2026. The Spirits & Biofuel business went to IGL Spirits Limited and Biopharma went to Ennature Bio Pharma Limited, and both are now separately listed.
The continuing business is Biobased Specialty Materials, Sustainable & Performance Chemicals and Gases.
read: Fact: the year-on-year drop is a scope change from the demerger, not a collapse in the business. Read: the only usable comparison is Q2 against Q1 FY27 on the restated base. Revenue was roughly flat (Rs. 358.18 crore against Rs. 354.64 crore). EBITDA and PAT slipped slightly (Rs. 39.34 crore against Rs. 40.21 crore, and Rs. 11.24 crore against Rs. 12.35 crore). By my arithmetic, EBITDA margin is about 11.0% against about 11.3%; the filing does not state it. The remaining company is much smaller than the old one, so the investment case now rests on the specialty and performance chemicals business and the demerged entities.
positives: Q2 revenue was stable on Q1 on the restated base
EBITDA and PAT were positive and close to Q1
Management says the demerger gives a sharper focus on bio-based specialities
risks: EBITDA and PAT slipped quarter on quarter with no explanation in the release
The release has no segment split, margin, debt, cash flow or guidance, so quality cannot be judged
Standalone and unaudited, and no like-for-like comparison is given
check_next: Get the full results filing: segment data, finance cost, debt allocated to the remaining company, other income, and any auditor limited-review remarks
Get restated FY26 and quarterly figures for the continuing business, and the share count behind EPS. Implied shares differ between Q2 FY27 and Q2 FY26, so check the share capital and the swap ratio
Check where the stock now trades against IGL Spirits and Ennature Bio Pharma, and what the exchange has adjusted for the demerger

headline: BHARATFORG: Wholly owned step-down arm Ferrovia Transrail merged into BF Infrastructure, effective Nov 17, 2026; both had NIL revenue in FY26
facts: Regional Director, Western Region order dated November 5, 2026 approved the merger of Ferrovia Transrail Solutions Private Limited (transferor) into BF Infrastructure Limited (transferee) under Section 233 of the Companies Act, 2013
The order was filed with the Registrar of Companies, Maharashtra on November 17, 2026, the date the Scheme became effective; the transferor is dissolved
Turnover/revenue from operations for year ended March 31, 2026: BFIL NIL; FTSPL NIL
BFIL holds 100% of FTSPL; no cash consideration and no new shares issued
Both entities are in EPC and infrastructure development projects
The company is not a party to the Scheme and its shareholding pattern is unchanged
read: This is an internal tidy-up inside the group. Both entities reported NIL revenue for FY26, so there is no effect on Bharat Forge's earnings, cash flow or share count. The stated rationale is synergy and lower operating cost, but with no revenue and no numbers given, any saving is not measurable from this filing.

read: This is a completed equity raise. The new shares are about 1.83% of the pre-issue share count (my calculation from the filing's share numbers), so dilution is small. The price was set about 3.3% above the floor, and the book was led by large, well-known institutions. The filing gives no size for the balance sheet, capital adequacy or the growth the capital funds, so I can't judge the effect on returns from this document alone. For a lender this is a capital top-up. Whether it matters depends on how much capital buffer it adds and whether it is used for growth.

Priced above the floor, with large institutions as top allottees
Raises growth and capital-adequacy headroom for a lender

Return on equity may dip until the new capital is deployed

headline: LIBAS: Q2 FY27 results carry a qualified review; auditor says inventory and profit overstated by ₹700.84 lakhs
facts: Standalone Q2 (30.09.2026) revenue from operations Rs 1,006.07 lakhs vs Rs 1,396.62 lakhs in 30.09.2025 and Rs 1,016.16 lakhs in 30.06.2026.

Standalone Q2 net profit Rs 51.62 lakhs vs Rs 50.60 lakhs a year ago. Basic EPS 0.20 vs 0.19. Half-year net profit Rs 142.99 lakhs vs a loss of Rs 158.30 lakhs (which included a Rs 240.00 lakhs fire-loss exceptional item).

Auditor J N Mital & Co gave a qualified conclusion on both standalone and consolidated results. In its opinion inventory is overstated by ₹700.84 lakhs of obsolete stock, and profit for the period is overstated by the same amount.
Auditor also flags that gratuity liability is not recognised, TDS returns for the first and second quarter were not filed, and matters from the FY26 annual report are 'still under process'.
Segment result (standalone, Q2): Rock Salt profit Rs 270.86 lakhs on revenue of Rs 526.91 lakhs. Garment loss Rs 156.64 lakhs on revenue of Rs 473.64 lakhs.

Standalone half-year operating cash flow Rs 10.34 lakhs against profit before tax of Rs 191.08 lakhs. Trade receivables Rs 4,088.15 lakhs, borrowings Rs 1,500.93 lakhs, cash Rs 6.88 lakhs. Consolidated Q2 net profit Rs 98.42 lakhs, EPS 0.57.
read: The headline profit is not reliable. The auditor says ₹700.84 lakhs of inventory is obsolete and profit is overstated by that amount. That is more than the half-year standalone profit of Rs 142.99 lakhs and about 13% of standalone equity of Rs 5,242.66 lakhs. If the auditor is right, the reported profit turns into a loss and the inventory and equity base shrink. Separately, revenue fell year on year and the garment segment is loss-making, while the profit comes from rock salt trading. Cash conversion is weak and receivables are about twice half-year revenue.
positives: Rock Salt segment profit rose to Rs 270.86 lakhs in Q2 from Rs 60.86 lakhs a year ago.
Standalone half-year profit is positive at Rs 142.99 lakhs, against a loss a year ago that included the fire-loss exceptional item.
Consolidated cash is Rs 869.43 lakhs against borrowings of Rs 1,500.93 lakhs.

headline: PARAMOUNT DYE TEC: H1 FY27 revenue Rs 3864.19 lakh, PAT Rs 138.05 lakh vs Rs 216.47 lakh a year ago; auditor flags unverified balances
facts: Half year ended 30 Sep 2026 (unaudited): revenue from operations Rs 3864.19 lakh, against Rs 3090.06 lakh in H1 FY26 and Rs 4289.48 lakh in H2 FY26.
Profit before tax Rs 170.31 lakh against Rs 244.55 lakh in H1 FY26. Profit after tax Rs 138.05 lakh against Rs 216.47 lakh. EPS Rs 1.99 against Rs 4.81.
Finance costs Rs 75.33 lakh against Rs 43.31 lakh in H1 FY26. Other income Rs 74.64 lakh.

Auditor (Rajesh Mehru & Co.) gave an emphasis of matter. It did no physical verification of inventory at 30 Sep 2026 and got no direct confirmations of receivables or payables. It relied on a CA certificate and management. The conclusion is not modified.

Net operating cash flow was Rs 804.47 lakh for the half year, against Rs -2175.41 lakh for FY26. Trade receivables rose to Rs 2668.19 lakh from Rs 1843.15 lakh at 31 Mar 2026. Inventory was Rs 3570.68 lakh.
Non-current borrowings rose to Rs 1197.09 lakh from Rs 217.99 lakh. Current borrowings fell to Rs 360.86 lakh from Rs 1427.28 lakh. Total equity was Rs 6710.75 lakh.
read: Fact: sales grew year on year but profit fell, so margins are thinner. By my arithmetic, PBT was about 4.4% of revenue against about 7.9% in H1 FY26. Read: the positive operating cash flow comes mostly from working-capital lines, not from profit. Other current assets and tax assets fell by Rs 1468.87 lakh and creditors rose by Rs 490.75 lakh, while receivables rose by Rs 825.05 lakh. The auditor's emphasis of matter means the inventory (Rs 3570.68 lakh) and receivables, which are the bulk of the assets, are not independently verified, so the quality of the numbers is the main issue. This is a small company with revenue below Rs 100 crore a year, so one half-year does not change the case unless the balances hold up.

Reported operating cash flow of Rs 804.47 lakh, a reversal from Rs -2175.41 lakh in FY26
Debt shifted from current to non-current, which eases near-term refinancing pressure

headline: SEYA INDUSTRIES: Q2 FY27 nil revenue, loss after tax ₹(1.77) lakh on other income ₹465.00 lakh; company still under CIRP
facts: Revenue from operations is nil for the quarter ended 30-Sep-26, the quarter ended 30-Jun-26 and the quarter ended 30-Sep-25. Other income is ₹465.00 lakh, against ₹381.00 lakh a year ago.
Loss before tax is ₹(56.75) lakh. A tax line of ₹(54.97) lakh brings loss after tax to ₹(1.77) lakh, against ₹(92.68) lakh a year ago and ₹(71.49) lakh last quarter. EPS is (0.01).
Depreciation is ₹444.91 lakh for the quarter. Finance cost is ₹0.00 lakh. Borrowings are ₹69,601.52 lakh non-current plus ₹7,696.65 lakh current.
Balance sheet at 30-Sep-26: capital work in progress ₹79,620.58 lakh, PPE ₹62,449.37 lakh, total equity ₹81,770.37 lakh. Cash is ₹82.13 lakh, unchanged from 31-Mar-26.
Note 1: the NCLT Mumbai ordered CIRP on November 2, 2023 on a Section 7 application by a financial creditor. The IRP approved the results on November 14, 2026.
The auditor's review report on the unaudited results has no qualification. The only segment is 'Speciality Chemical Intermediates'.
read: This is a shell-like set of results. The company has had no operating revenue for at least two years of comparisons, and the quarter's near-breakeven loss comes from other income and a tax credit. Finance cost is about nil against roughly ₹77,298 lakh of borrowings (₹69,601.52 lakh non-current plus ₹7,696.65 lakh current). That is presumably because of the CIRP, but it means reported losses understate the economic burden. The investment case rests on the resolution outcome, not on these numbers.
positives: Loss after tax narrowed to ₹(1.77) lakh from ₹(92.68) lakh a year ago
Review report carries no qualification
Assets on the balance sheet are large (₹1,60,509.84 lakh) against equity of ₹81,770.37 lakh
risks: CIRP since November 2, 2023, with no revenue. Equity holders usually rank last in a resolution, and a haircut or extinguishment is possible.

headline: INTLCONV: Q2FY27 consolidated revenue ₹82.4 Cr (+81.9% YoY), EBITDA ₹23.1 Cr, but PAT still a loss of ₹0.7 Cr on treasury mark-to-market
facts: Q2FY27 consolidated revenue from operations ₹82.4 Cr vs ₹45.3 Cr in Q2FY26, up 81.9% YoY
Q2FY27 EBITDA (excluding other income) ₹23.1 Cr vs ₹10.8 Cr, up 113.6%. EBITDA margin 28.0% vs 23.9%
Q2FY27 PAT was -₹0.7 Cr vs -₹17.4 Cr in Q2FY26. The note says profitability was impacted by mark-to-market movements in treasury investments
H1FY27 PAT of ₹119.1 Cr is larger than H1 revenue of ₹117.7 Cr. The release shows H1 PAT margin as 101.2%

The release says results were announced on November 13, 2026. The press release is dated November 17, 2026. The CMD cites North American shipments, a healthy order book, European customer trials and Mineplast Pro
read: The operating business improved sharply. Q2 revenue rose 81.9% and EBITDA margin widened to 28.0%, helped by North American shipments. The headline 'net profit up 243.2%' is not an operating number. H1 PAT of ₹119.1 Cr exceeds H1 revenue of ₹117.7 Cr, which points to large treasury investment gains, mostly in Q1 (my inference from H1 minus Q2). Q2 PAT was still a loss of ₹0.7 Cr. Reported profit therefore swings with the investment book, and EBITDA is the cleaner guide to the core business. Q2 revenue and EBITDA are also well above the implied Q1 (revenue about ₹35.3 Cr, EBITDA about ₹7.1 Cr, both derived), so lumpy export shipments are a possible explanation.
positives: Q2 EBITDA more than doubled to ₹23.1 Cr, with margin up from 23.9% to 28.0%
Management cites a healthy order book, entry into new mining segments with Mineplast Pro and European customer progress
H1 operating growth is real: revenue +45.8%, EBITDA +86.3%
risks: Earnings quality: PAT is dominated by treasury mark-to-market, and the swing between a Q1 gain and a Q2 loss shows how volatile it is
Lumpiness: Q2 looks well above the implied Q1 (about ₹35.3 Cr revenue, derived), so it may reflect shipment timing rather than a steady run-rate
The release gives no order book value, no segment or export split, no balance sheet and no cash flow. The headline PAT growth figure can mislead
check_next: Read the full results filing: Q1 and Q2 split, other income, treasury gains and losses, tax, and the size of the investment portfolio against net worth
Check the order book value, export share, North American customer concentration and any tariff exposure, and whether Q2 shipments were one-off
Check H1 operating cash flow, receivable and inventory days, and any auditor limited-review remarks. Also ask why the press release came four days after the results

headline: ION EXCHANGE: CRISIL cuts outlook to Negative from Stable, keeps A+/A1; H1FY27 Ebitda margin -3.8%, PAT Rs -80 crore
facts: CRISIL revised the long-term outlook to Negative from Stable and reaffirmed CRISIL A+. Short-term CRISIL A1 reaffirmed. Rated bank facilities total INR 2099.74 Crore.
CRISIL's stated reasons: one-time provisions on key large legacy EPC projects, higher raw material prices hurting chemical margins, and a slower-than-expected ramp-up of the Roha Plant.

H1FY27 consolidated revenue grew 4.5% on-year to Rs 1,375 crore. Operating margin was negative 3.8%, against 9.9% in H1FY26. Crisil-adjusted PAT was Rs -80 crore. Adjusted interest coverage was -2.5 times.
Treatment solutions revenue fell 25% on-year to Rs 360 crore, on delayed Middle East projects and revenue reversals. The one-time provision on 2-3 legacy projects was around Rs 90 crore.
CRISIL estimates FY27 revenue at ~Rs 3,000 crore with operating margin of 4-5%. FY26 operating income was Rs 2915 crore and PAT Rs 143.2 crore.

Gearing was 0.4 time at September 30, 2026: networth ~Rs 1,225 crore against debt of Rs 443 crore. Unencumbered standalone cash was ~Rs 120 crore. Engineering order book was Rs 2,969 crore (Rs 2,830 crore a year earlier).
read: The rating itself is intact. The outlook change matters because it confirms a sharp H1 deterioration: a loss at the operating level, with a ~Rs 90 crore legacy-project provision equal to about 6.5% of H1 revenue. Balance sheet strength is the cushion, with low gearing, Rs 120 crore of cash and 40-45% utilisation of fund-based limits. FY27 guidance of 4-5% margin on ~Rs 3,000 crore implies a weak year, well below the FY26 PAT of Rs 143.2 crore. Legacy EPC cost overruns, receivables of 142 days and ~Rs 860 crore of bank guarantees are the quality concerns.
positives: A+ and A1 reaffirmed; gearing 0.4 time and liquidity described as strong
Chemical and industrial products revenue grew 19% and 25% on-year, to Rs 484 crore and Rs 241 crore
Order book Rs 2,969 crore, up from Rs 2,830 crore; bid pipeline ~Rs 9,300 crore
risks: Legacy EPC cost escalations 'not factored in earlier' (~Rs 90 crore). This is a quality-of-execution and provisioning red flag, and more provisions are possible
Working capital is heavy: gross current assets 283 days, receivables 142 days. Contingent liabilities are ~Rs 860 crore of LC/bank guarantees
Chemical margin hit by crude-linked inputs, with the Roha ramp-up slower than planned. A further downgrade would follow if TOL/TNW goes above 2 times or margins fall further
check_next: Read the H1FY27 results and the cash flow statement: operating cash flow, provision details, and whether the Rs 90 crore is truly one-time

Check the Roha plant utilisation and the chemical segment margin outlook. Also check the CRISIL text 'Ebit margin ~10% during the second half of fiscal 2027', which cannot be actual data as of Nov 202
Look at the status of the Middle East projects and the legacy projects: remaining unbilled or disputed amounts, and bank guarantee invocation risk
